title: AVO meter — resistance measurement
content:
C. RESISTANCE MEASUREMENT

To measure voltage the selector switch is turned to measure ohms. The leads are connected across the resistance to be measured as shown in figure 13.31. The battery supplies the current to the galvanometer for deflection. Since the amount of current through the galvanometer now depends upon the external resistance the scale can be calibrated in ohms.

FIGURE 13.31 — AVO meter switch turned to resistance measurement

title: Digital multimeters and Figure 13.32
content:
The amount of deflection in the galvanometer will now show the resistance directly. The ohm-meter reading does not depends upon the polarity of the terminal leads, because the direction of current through the galvanometer is determined by the polarity of the battery.

I. DIGITAL MULTI-METERS

Modern multimeters come with digital display, accurate, reliable, durable and have added extra features. It is also easy to use because values are displayed automatically in decimal with proper units. Thus the human errors (such as parallax) in reading the detail of the ordinary AVO meter are eliminated.

In these devices instead of ordinary galvanometer the integrated circuit electronically controls all the functions. Modern digital multimeters make use of computer software, which provides other functions as well, increasing the scope of using a multimeter.

title: Unit 13 key points
content:
KEY POINTS

Force on a current carrying conductor in a magnetic filed: A Current carrying wire has a magnetic field around it. When this field interacts with external magnetic field there is a force on it, which is given by F = I L × B

Magnetic flux: The scalar product of magnetic induction vector B and the area ΔA, mathematically ΔΦ_B = B⃗ • ΔA⃗ = BΔA cosθ

Ampere’s Law: This law relates the integrated magnetic field in a loop around a current carrying wire to the current passing through the wire. ΣB.Δl = μ₀I

The magnetic field of a solenoid: The magnetic field of a solenoid is given by B= n μ₀ I

Force on a charged particle in magnetic field: The force acting on the charged particle results from the interaction of the external magnetic field and the magnetic field created by the moving charge.

Velocity selector: The device which allow only the particles with certain specific speed through it (thus permitting particles only with selected speeds)

Torque on a current carrying coil in a magnetic field: Torque on a current carrying coil in magnetic field is τ = NIAB sin θ

Galvanometer: A device used for detection and measurement of small electric currents

Shunt resistance: The low resistance connected in parallel with galvanometer, mathematically R_s = I_gR_g/(I − I_g)

High resistance: The high value resistance connected in series with galvanometer, mathematically R_h = V/I_g − R_g

AVO Meter: A single device which can measure current, voltage and resistance.

د امپیر قانون: دا قانون د جریان‌لرونکي سیم په شاوخوا کړۍ کې انتګرالي مقناطیسي ساحه په سیم کې له تېرېدونکي جریان سره تړي: ∑ B⃗ · Δl⃗ = μ₀ I.

title: Unit 13 exercise — multiple-choice questions 1–14
content:
Choose the best possible answer

1. A current is flowing North in a magnetic field that points West. It experiences A. a force down. B. a force up. C. a force west. D. no force .

2. Two long, straight wires have currents flowing in them in the same direction, the force between the wires is A. attractive. B. repulsive. C. zero. D. infinite

3. One weber is equal to A. N A²/m B. N m²/A C. N A/m D. N m/A

4. Magnetic flux will be maximum if the angle between magnetic field strength and vector area is A. 0° B. 45° C. 60° D. 90°

5. Ampere’s law is applied over any A. surface B. closed surface C. path D. closed path

6. When the number of turns in a solenoid is doubled without any change in the length of the solenoid its self induction will be A. Four times B. Doubled C. Halved D. One forth

7. If the charge is at rest in magnetic field, then force on charge is A. qvB B. qvB cos θ C. qvB sin θ D. zero

8. Work done on a charge particle moving in a uniform magnetic field is A. maximum B. minimum C. zero. D. infinite

9. The Earths northern magnetic pole acts like: A. the north pole of a magnet B. the south pole of a magnet C. it has a positive charge D. it has a negative charge

10. The pole pieces of the magnet in galvanometer are made concave to make the field A. Radial B. Stronger C. Weaker D. Both A & B

11. When a small resistance is connected parallel to galvanometer, the resulting circuit behaves as A. Voltmeter B. Ammeter C. Velocity Selector D. AVO meter

12. To measure the voltage the voltmeter is connected with the circuit in A. series B. parallel C. Perpendicular D. Straight Line

13. The resistance of ideal voltmeter is A. Small B. Large C. Zero D. Infinite

14. The torque in the coil can be increased by increasing A. Number of turns B. Current and magnetic field C. Area of coil D. All of these

title: Unit 13 exercise — conceptual questions 1–9
content:
CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS

1. A compass needle is deflected when a charged plastic rod is held near it. What is the origin of the force that produces the deflection?

2. What is the difference between permeability and permittivity?

3. Can the objects in rotational motion create a magnetic field? Provide an example.

4. Electron and proton are projected with the same velocity normal to the magnetic field. Which one will suffer greater deflection? Why?

5. A charged particle moves in a straight line through a particular region of space. Could there be a non-zero magnetic field in this region?

6. If a current is passed through an unstretched spring, will the spring contract or expand?

7. How can neutrons be accelerated in a cyclotron?

8. A current carrying loop, free to turn, is placed in a uniform magnetic field B. What will be its orientation relative to B, in the equilibrium state?

9. How does a current carrying coil behave like a bar magnet?

title: Unit 13 exercise — numerical problems 1–10
content:
NUMERICAL PROBLEMS

1. At what distance from a long straight wire carrying a current of 10 A is the magnetic field is equal to the earth’s magnetic field of 5 × 10⁻⁵ T? (Answer: 0.04 m)

2. A long solenoid having 1000 turns uniformly distributed over a length of 0.5 m produces a magnetic field of 2.5 × 10⁻³ T at the center. Find the current in the solenoid. (Answer: 1 A)
